text: Fixture Bank Limited — Framework Alignment — DGI
One assessment, four vocabularies. These are not four independent measurements — they are one evidence base expressed in four published
frameworks. The four overall figures landing close together is the correct result: the same answers, projected through the same eleven capability
pillars. What differs between them is emphasis and structure, which is what makes each one legible to a different audience.
Retained share is how much of the framework’s own definition of a dimension is in scope under this engagement’s layer. Scored share is how
much of what is in scope was actually measured. They answer different questions and are never combined: a dimension can be fully retained
and barely scored, or the reverse, and a single "coverage" number would hide whichever is worse.
All figures are on the DGIW 1-5 maturity scale. They are NOT rescaled to each framework’s own scale — DCAM scores 1-6 and COBIT 2019
uses capability levels 0-5. A DCAM component shown here as 3.2 is 3.2 out of 5, not out of 6.
What is published and what is ours
Framework names, codes and dimension structures are published content. The relative WEIGHTS applied to those dimensions
are Godaitec editorial judgement — none of these four frameworks publishes weightings for its own dimensions. The weights are
the first thing to challenge in review, and changing them changes every figure derived from them.
DGI (Ten-component framework) — Published structure recorded at MEDIUM-HIGH confidence — verify before relying on it in an audit context.
The ten components are well documented and I am confident in them. The three groupings used here as parents — Rules & Rules of
Engagement, People & Organizational Bodies, Processes — are how the published DGI diagram arranges those ten; I am treating a
presentational grouping as a formal level, which is a modelling choice rather than published hierarchy. Flagged because a reviewer may
reasonably want the ten flat. DGI publishes no maturity scale; 1-5 is DGIW's.

Why each dimension maps to the capabilities it does
Every row below was authored deliberately. A mapping a consultant cannot defend in a room is not a mapping, and this section is the room.
Mission and vision for data governance is the strategy statement P02 assesses.
DGI02 · Goals, Governance Metrics, Success Measures & Funding Strategies
Goals, success measures and funding strategy are strategy-level commitments, P02.
Governance metrics are reported into and acted on by the governance forum, which P01 measures.
Data definitions are the glossary; P04 asks whether they exist, are agreed and are used.
DGI's 'data rules' are business rules that become quality rules — the substance of P05.
Rules that constrain structure are architectural standards, P03.
In a bank, the contested definitions are product, GL and counterparty hierarchies — reference data
governance, P06. Banking-only, so DGI03 retains 0.90 under core.
Decision rights are P01's defining subject. A clean one-to-one.

Accountabilities map wholly onto P01 — who owns what, and what follows when they do not.
DGI's controls are predominantly protective and access controls, P08.
Data-content controls are quality controls, measured in P05.
Control ownership and the escalation path when a control fails is P01.
Identifying and engaging stakeholders is operating-model work — who sits in the forum and who is
Stakeholder engagement is also how the mandate is sustained, which P02 assesses.
The DG Office as a structural element of the operating model — its constitution, its place in the forum
hierarchy and its decision rights — is P01. This was authored at 1.00 as 'a clean one-to-one'; that was
true of the office's EXISTENCE and wrong about the component, which also covers how the office is
funded and what it operates. Reduced to 0.60 with the remainder mapped explicitly.
DGI's DGO component covers the office's mandate and funding strategy, not only its structure. A DG
Office that cannot fund itself past the next budget cycle is the failure P02 measures, and nothing else
in the DGI crosswalk reaches it.
The DGO is the operator of the catalogue, quality engine and lineage collection. A governance tool at
8% population is a DGO capacity finding that gets misread as a tooling problem, and P10 is where it
Stewardship as a role — appointment, mandate, time allocation — is P01.
What stewards actually do day to day is triage and remediate quality issues, which P05 measures.
DGI10 · Proactive, Reactive and Ongoing Data Governance Processes
The governance processes themselves — issue escalation, exception handling, change — are P01.
DGI's 'reactive' processes are predominantly data quality issue management, P05.
'Ongoing' processes include retention, archival and disposal cycles, which DGIW measures in P09.

What this assessment does not cover
Every leaf dimension of DGI is both in scope under this layer and measured. Nothing in the framework is unaddressed.
DCAM is modelled at v2.2. Its capability and sub-capability levels beneath each component are deliberately NOT authored: they were not
recalled reliably enough to put in front of an auditor, and an absent level is recoverable where an invented one is not. DCAM v3.0
reorganised the model and is not what is represented here.
COBIT 2019 APO14 sub-practice titles have been checked against a public COBIT 2019 reference and corrected where they differed. They
have NOT been checked against the ISACA publication itself, which is the only source an audit function should accept — treat them as
verified secondhand, not as quoted. The five EDM governance objectives are high confidence.
The three DGI groupings used as parents are how the published DGI diagram arranges the ten components; treating that arrangement as a
formal level is a modelling choice, not published hierarchy.
